notes: Gold = main sources only (*/src/main/scala and */src/main/java), tests, sbt-test fixtures and documentation snippets excluded. Mostly Scala internals (filters, evolutions, server backends, body parsers, cache, routes compiler); one impact task crosses into the Java API (Scala method called from a Java action). Scala-specific constructs in the gold: methods of anonymous classes (findAssetPath), private[play] classes nested in companion objects (JWTFormatter), vals (Evolution.hash, cachingWithEternity) and traits. Generic method names (apply, parse, handleResult) are avoided as gold names when a class name identifies the unit better. `search` is the phrase an agent would derive from the question (English, no identifier the developer did not give). Re-check with `kopt bench playframework --verify`.

tasks.question: When an evolution script that was already applied to the database is edited, where does Play detect the change and decide to run its Downs and then its Ups again?
tasks.search: evolution script modified already applied hash conflict downs ups
tasks.verifiedBy: Read @3.0.12: DatabaseEvolutions.scripts(evolutions) (EvolutionsApi.scala:311) splits database and application evolutions into non-conflicting downs/ups and the overlapping rest, then calls Evolutions.conflictings (Evolutions.scala:205), which zips the overlapping pairs, reverses them and drops pairs whose Evolution.hash (Evolutions.scala:41, sha1 of trimmed downs + ups) is equal, so every revision from the first edited one is reverted (DownScript) then re-applied (UpScript).

tasks.question: When the CSRF filter has to find the token in a POSTed url-encoded or multipart form body, where is the body buffered and the token extracted and compared before the action is allowed to run?
tasks.search: csrf token form body multipart extract buffer before action
tasks.verifiedBy: Read CSRFActions.scala@3.0.12: CSRFAction.apply dispatches form-urlencoded bodies to checkFormBody and multipart bodies to checkMultipartBody, both built on checkBody (159), which pipes the body through a BodyHandler graph stage (321, buffers up to postBodyBuffer, then validates and fails the stage with NoTokenInBody on a missing or wrong token) whose callback extracts the token with extractTokenFromFormBody (207) or extractTokenFromMultipartFormDataBody (227) and compares it with tokenProvider.compareTokens; the action only runs on the validated body source.

tasks.question: Where does Play reject a session cookie whose JWT is expired, not yet valid (with clock skew) or signed with another algorithm, and where does it still accept old URL-encoded signed session cookies?

tasks.verifiedBy: Read Cookie.scala@3.0.12: JWTCookieDataCodec (629) decode() calls the formatter and maps PrematureJwtException, ExpiredJwtException, SignatureException and algorithm mismatches to an empty session; JWTCookieDataCodec.JWTFormatter (718) builds the jjwt parser with the clock and setAllowedClockSkewSeconds; JWTFormatter.parse (752) throws IllegalStateException when the header algorithm differs from the configured one; FallbackCookieDataCodec (843) decodes values containing '=' with the legacy URL-encoded signed codec and values containing '.' as JWT.

tasks.question: How does the gzip filter decide whether to compress a response, and when does it buffer the whole body versus stream it chunked (including the HTTP/1.0 case)?
tasks.search: gzip filter compress response threshold chunked accept encoding
tasks.verifiedBy: Read GzipFilter.scala@3.0.12: apply only wraps requests for which mayCompress (152: not HEAD) and gzipIsAcceptedAndPreferredBy (155: gzip q-value > 0 and >= identity) hold; handleResult (77) compresses when shouldCompress (170: not 204/304, no Content-Encoding, not known empty, length > threshold) and config.shouldGzip: strict bodies and streamed bodies with a known length <= chunkedThreshold are buffered and compressed whole, larger streams become close-delimited for HTTP/1.0 or chunked otherwise, and chunked bodies go through a gzip flow that keeps the last chunk.

tasks.question: Behind proxies that send X-Forwarded-For or RFC 7239 Forwarded headers, how does Play work out the client's real IP address and whether the request was secure, and which proxies does it trust?
tasks.search: forwarded headers x-forwarded-for trusted proxies remote address secure
tasks.verifiedBy: Read ForwardedHeaderHandler.scala@3.0.12: forwardedConnection (67) returns a RemoteConnection whose lazily computed value scans the entries of ForwardedHeaderHandlerConfig.forwardedHeaders (167: x-forwarded or rfc7239 version) from the nearest proxy backwards; while the previous hop isTrustedProxy (240: matches play.http.forwarded.trustedProxies subnets) it moves to the next entry parsed by parseEntry (217: address plus proto=https -> secure), otherwise it stops and keeps the previous connection.

tasks.question: How does the `Cached` action helper of play-cache answer 304 Not Modified, serve a cached result, or run the action and store its result together with ETag and Expires headers?
tasks.search: Cached action result cache etag expires not modified
tasks.verifiedBy: Read Cached.scala@3.0.12: CachedBuilder.build (146) computes resultKey and resultKey-etag, returns NotModified when If-None-Match is * or contains the cached ETag, else serves the cached SerializableResult, else runs the action and maps it through handleResult (209), which (only for headers matched by the caching partial function, wrapped by cachingWithEternity (199) so that a zero duration means one year) sets Expires and an ETag = quoted sha1 of the expiration date, and stores both the ETag and the result in the AsyncCacheApi.

tasks.question: In the assets controller, which code calls `digest` to look up the fingerprint of an asset?
tasks.verifiedBy: Read Assets.scala@3.0.12 and git grep 'digest(': DefaultAssetsMetadata.digest (444) reads <path>.<digestAlgorithm> and caches it; callers: findAssetPath (424, method of the anonymous AssetsFinder of DefaultAssetsMetadata, prefixes the file name with the digest for reverse routing), assetInfoFromResource (484, stores the digest in AssetInfo for the ETag), AssetsBuilder.versioned(path, file) (794, compares the requested fingerprint with digest(bareFullPath) to enable aggressive caching) and StaticAssetsMetadata (303) whose digest override forwards to its delegate.
